subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
I should aim for a compact but complete module using the SDK. I'm planning a six-wheeled heavy carrier design: a long hull with a front cab, a railgun turret mounted on the back, and four deployable outrigger stabiliser legs.

For the rig, I'll set up a chassis root joint with wheel joints, outrigger joints, and turret yaw/pitch/rail joints, keeping everything oriented along +Z and grounded at y=0. I'm planning to build the parts using boxes, rods, sweeps, extrusions, and lathes, applying custom paint with noise texture for the hull plus decal planes for stencils, hazard stripes, and emblems, and I'll avoid unfamiliar kit imports in favor of simpler custom materials.

Now I'm working out joint placement: wheel joints spin around an axle axis, while the four outrigger legs extend diagonally outward from the chassis with horizontal arms and vertical hydraulic jacks down to ground pads. I'm positioning three wheel axles front-to-back along the z-axis to balance the vehicle's stance.

I'm also sizing the hull and cab — setting the chassis width so the wheels sit outboard, defining deck height, and shaping the front cab region as a wedge extending upward and forward.

For the railgun, I'm working out a rear turret mount with a pitch joint so the barrel can elevate rather than collide with the cab roof, trying a forward-up angle around 20 degrees and checking the clearance over the cab at that pitch.

Defining direction and up vectors for the barrel, then setting up helper functions to place boxes aligned along the z-axis and cylinders aligned along the barrel direction for the rods.

Now I'm sketching the railgun structure itself—twin rails with a glowing core strip, capacitor drums, coil rings, muzzle shroud, breech housing with bolts and hazard stripes, plus the turret's yaw/pitch joints, cheek plates, trunnions, and elevation cylinders connecting to hull armor panels.

Moving to rear details: capacitor banks behind the turret, radiator vents and exhaust stacks for the power plant, then the wheel assembly with treaded tires, rims, hubs, lug nuts, fenders using partial cylinder geometry, and mud flaps. For the cab, I'm planning a lower box with an upper frustum, sloped windscreen glass, armored window shutters, and glowing headlights with a light bar.

Now I'm adding the bull bar bumper with tow hooks, a roof sensor dome, antenna, door handles, a step, and a decal texture for numbering and an emblem. For the stabilizer legs, I'm working out placement—arm, hydraulic cylinder, wide pad, ribbed foot, chain, warning stripes, and a glowing lamp—positioning four legs outside the wheel track near the front and rear of the chassis.

I'm now designing the hull paint shader, building a layered color function with base olive-grey tones, mottling, countershading, panel seam lines, and dirt darkening near the bottom.

For textures, I'm planning hazard stripe patterns, stencil text labels like "R-07", a lightning emblem, warning triangles, and rail labels, rendered as plane geometry with SVG-based patterns for the hazard stripes.

I'm sketching out helper functions for box and cylinder geometry, a mirroring utility for symmetric parts, a glow effect for lights, and a bolt-ring generator that places fasteners around a face using frame math.

Now I'm working out the wheel construction logic, defining the axle orientation and tire geometry as a low-poly cylinder shape.

Placing 16 tread blocks around the tire, sizing them so they sit flush with the hub radius without poking through the floor, and figuring out the rotation needed so each block's long axis points radially outward at its angle position.

I'm reconsidering the block count to keep part totals manageable—dropping to 12 angles with 2 blocks each per wheel (24 per wheel, 144 across all six wheels), estimating total parts stay under 1000. To save further on part count, I'm planning to merge each wheel's tread blocks into a single geometry using matrix transforms before merging, keeping the wheel spin bone simple at the origin.

Writing merge helper logic...

Adding the core glow strip between rails, ring clamp insulators every 1.2m, and glowing capacitor drums mounted along both sides of the gun barrel.

I'm dropping the coil-ring idea and instead adding ribbed heat-sink fins on the rails, a muzzle shroud with a dark glowing hole, recoil buffer cylinders under the breech, and a top-mounted sight. I'm setting up the local coordinate helper functions using forward and up vectors tilted at the gun's elevation angle to position everything relative to the barrel's orientation.

Now I'm working out hydraulic elevation rams connecting the turret base to the gun's underside, modeling each as a two-piece rod with a cylinder segment on the yaw bone and a piston segment on the pitch bone.

Next I'm turning to the turret itself: placing the yaw joint and pivot point, building the drum as a short cylinder, adding box-shaped cheeks on either side, trunnion cylinders along the X axis, and an armor housing shell below, plus a hatch and sensor dome on top. I'm double-checking that the cheek spacing clears the gun's width so nothing clips.

Then I'm moving to the rear hull, placing a power module box behind the turret with radiator vents, exhaust stacks, and a glowing cell panel, making sure it sits clear of the turret pivot and barrel swing, before sketching the mid-hull deck box and side skirts.

Building hull side profile extrusion...

I'm refining the windscreen profile coordinates and checking clearance between the cab width and the wheel positions—narrowing the cab width slightly so it doesn't collide with the wheel hubs, then planning to add fenders over them.

Now I'm noticing the hull also overlaps the wheels at certain heights, so I'll shrink the hull half-width and raise its bottom clearance above the wheels, adding separate fender/sponson boxes to cover the wheels instead of relying on the hull shape itself.

Adding undercarriage details now—axles, differential spheres, driveshaft, and suspension arms linking chassis to hubs, plus shock absorbers with coil rings. For the cab, I'm working out the raked windscreen geometry and placing window planes against the angled front face.

Adding more cab details...

Still detailing the jack mechanism...

Now I'm thinking about adding a rear recoil spade plate angled at the back of the vehicle for extra stability.

I'm also planning the texture set: hazard stripes, an ID number, an emblem, a warning triangle, and a label reading "RAILGUN MK IV."

I'm sketching a decal helper function that places flat planes slightly above the surface with a texture, bone, position, and direction, so I can attach markings anywhere on the hull. For wheels, I'm using dark flat rubber for tires and lighter metal tones for rims, and for the hull I'm setting up an olive base camo paint with mottled patches in varying shades for a weathered military look.

Now I'm building a custom paint function that layers dirt and grime onto the camo base: resolving the camo color at each surface point, then blending in brownish dirt tones based on height and noise, with heavier buildup lower on the hull and lighter coloring toward the top.

I'm also adding panel seams by checking position modulo a repeat interval along the z-axis and darkening those thin seam lines when the surface normal is roughly horizontal. I plan to reuse this same hull paint across other components like sponsons and turret for a continuous camo look, and I'm defining a steel color palette (dark, gunmetal, light steel) for the metal parts.

Expanding the palette with brass, amber, cyan energy, glass, red, and white stencil colors, and deciding to use rng sparingly for small greeble scatter on the power module. Now I'm starting to write the actual import statements, pulling in builder functions and the glow kit along with geometry merging utilities.

Writing builder helpers...

Writing the wheel function...

Still writing tread geometry...

Adding radial rib geometry and wheel hub details, then sketching suspension components like swing arms, shocks, and axle housings connecting the wheels to the chassis.

Adding stowage boxes...

I should move the stowage to the deck to avoid clashing with the skirt plates, then start writing the actual geometry code, keeping the rod and spike helper signatures straight and extruding the hull shape along the right axes.

Continuing to set up outline points for the hull and cab, marking corners sharp, then working out decal plane orientations so text faces outward correctly on both sides of the vehicle.

Now I'm placing roof details on the cab—light bar, beacon, antennas, and a sensor dome—then moving to the turret's housing roof, hatch, and the railgun's targeting camera.

Adding hull deck features...

Adding more clamps and lugs...

Adding more cannon details...

Continuing to lay out turret housing and cheek boxes around the yaw pivot, plus a flat base ring torus for the mount.

Realizing the torus radius is too wide for the current hull deck, so I need to widen the upper deck plate to around 2.9 units to properly support the turret ring without it overhanging the hull sides.

I'm repositioning the skirt panels to sit just outside the wheel tops without clipping the tires, adjusting them to cover the wheel arch region from y1.25 to 1.78 and using them as functional fenders instead of adding separate fender geometry.

Adding fender boxes over the wheels and angled plates, then checking the hull extrusion sits beneath the deck slab without clipping. Now I'm placing the turret ring on the deck top with a yaw joint and sizing the housing box above it.

Reworking the housing center and pivot height so the gun cheeks and barrel geometry line up, then recomputing the barrel tip position and verifying clearance between the barrel and the cab at the sides.

Checking for collisions between the roof rails, antenna, light bar, and the barrel sweep at different widths—they all clear each other both laterally and vertically. The turret housing fits fine on the hull deck, and total height including the muzzle stays reasonable, so now I'm adding rear deck details like the power module slab and exhaust stacks.

I'm laying out the rest of the deck now—radiators, hatches, ammo cassettes, cab connection, rear spade, tail lights, and tow pintle. Then I'm writing the hazard-stripe pattern SVG texture...

Now I'm defining a vehicle number decal with bold stroked text and sketching out a circular shield-and-bolt emblem badge.

I'm working through wheel naming and axle positions, plus deciding whether to add steering hinge joints for the front axles before finalizing the rig structure.
